title: Brick stitch trivet
subtitle: A 15 cm square table trivet in five-colour brick stitch on 13-count canvas
excerpt: A firm square trivet in brick stitch on 13-count canvas, worked in five shades of terracotta and ochre. The offset row layout of brick stitch gives this piece a tiled appearance. The finished canvas is mounted over a cork tile for rigidity.
sourceNotes: Brick stitch construction derived from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), straight canvas stitch chapter. Colour scheme synthesised from tile motifs in Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: A standard domestic cork floor tile used as a rigid, heat-tolerant backing for a needlepoint trivet. Glued or laced to the reverse of the finished canvas.

heroPrompt: A square needlepoint trivet in terracotta and ochre brick stitch pattern, sitting on a kitchen table with a small teapot on it, natural light.

content.text: This trivet is a 78 by 78 hole square on 13-count canvas, worked in brick stitch in five shades of terracotta, ochre, and sand. Each stitch is upright over two threads. Alternate rows are offset by one thread, giving the characteristic tiled pattern. The finished canvas is mounted over a cork tile for heat resistance and rigidity.
What you need

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas, cut 26 by 26 cm (leaves a 5 cm margin around the 78 by 78 hole design)

items.label: Thread: shade 1 (darkest)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 356 / Anchor 5975 (medium terra cotta). About 4 m

items.label: Thread: shade 2
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 758 / Anchor 9575 (light terra cotta). About 4 m

items.label: Thread: shade 3
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 407 / Anchor 914 (medium desert sand). About 4 m

items.label: Thread: shade 4
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 950 / Anchor 4146 (light desert sand). About 4 m

items.label: Thread: shade 5 (lightest)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 739 / Anchor 366 (ultra light tan). About 4 m

items.label: Cork tile
items.value: Standard 15 cm square cork floor tile, 3–4 mm thick

items.label: Strong thread
items.value: Linen or button thread for lacing the canvas over the tile

content.text: Palette
Shade 1: DMC 356 / Anchor 5975: medium terra cotta
Shade 2: DMC 758 / Anchor 9575: light terra cotta
Shade 3: DMC 407 / Anchor 914: medium desert sand
Shade 4: DMC 950 / Anchor 4146: light desert sand
Shade 5: DMC 739 / Anchor 366: ultra light tan
Stretching the canvas
Mount on a scroll frame. Brick stitch causes less diagonal distortion than tent stitch, but a frame keeps the horizontal rows running straight.
Stitches used
Brick stitch
: upright stitches over two threads, offset by one thread between rows.
Working method
Work the first row across the full 78-hole width in Shade 1. Each stitch is over two threads, placed every two holes across the row.
Work the second row in Shade 2, offset so each stitch starts one thread below the midpoint of the stitch above.
Continue cycling through the five shades for each row, repeating the cycle.
Fill all 78 rows. Block the canvas by dampening and pinning square to a board overnight.
Finishing
Lace the blocked canvas over the
cork tile backing

: fold the canvas margins to the back of the tile and lace tightly with strong thread in both directions. The cork provides heat resistance for use as a trivet. Do not glue; lacing allows the canvas to be replaced without destroying the tile.
What to try next
A Hungarian stitch layout using the same five-colour cycling produces a diamond lattice instead of a brick pattern on the same canvas size.
